articles.title: 是夜速报：德·斯瓦特的自然与丰饶之声
articles.original_title: 是夜速报：德·斯瓦特的自然与丰饶之声

translations.zh:
巴黎这几天气温骤降，每天早上起来眺望窗外都能看到楼下的公园草地结了一层白霜，太阳落山之后尤甚。走在前往爱乐大厅的路上冷气阵阵，加之巴黎政府为了环保将路灯换成了LED照明，除了路灯下那一小块圆形光斑之外整条街道漆黑一片，爱乐大厅门口的公园更是暗得连植物的剪影都

变得模糊不清，令人不禁想到乔治·桑笔下的法国冬天

：黑暗吞噬了一切，寒冷的夜

风在树间呼啸。巴黎爱乐大厅的旧厅音乐城

（Cité de la musique）

的红色走廊就矗立在黑暗的尽头，穿过走廊便是暖气开得十足的音乐厅。

今夜的演出是法国才华横溢的巴洛克小提琴新星泰奥蒂姆·朗格卢瓦·德·斯瓦特

（Théotime Langlois de Swarte）

和他的乐团Le

Consort带来的维瓦尔第和

乔瓦尼·勒格伦齐

（Giovanni Legrenzi）

的作品。和当前法国众多优秀的巴洛克音乐家一样，德·斯瓦特出身威廉·克里斯蒂

（William Christie）

创立的繁花古乐团

（Les Arts Florissants）

。本次他所用的小提琴他多次在录音中所使用的由雅各布·斯坦纳

（Jacob Steiner）

于1665年制作的小提琴以及皮埃尔·图尔特

（Pierre Tourte）

制作的弓。

难以想象，这是95年生人能演奏出的水平

音乐会以勒格伦齐的歌剧《宇宙的分裂

（La divisione del mondo）

》中的一首咏叹调作为开场，这首复调柔和宁静，德·斯瓦特的演奏线条悠长。作为维瓦尔第的老师之一，勒格伦齐对音乐发展有着具有决定性的贡献：他是首位采用三乐章结构奏鸣曲的作曲家——这一形式在后期逐渐定型并且得到了广泛应用。远在莱比锡的巴赫亦受其影响颇深，甚至还创作了一首以其为主题的赋格BWV 574。

本次音乐会的重点曲目是维瓦尔第的《四季》，在演出《春》乐章前，德·斯瓦特做了一小段介绍，他说这套曲目早就被演到路人皆知，他也不多作介绍，只是希望大家听一下他重新配器的版本——也是他明天（1月17日）即将发行的新专辑的内容。

自哈农库特

（Nikolaus Harnoncourt）

在1977年推出了一版在当时充满争议而如今看来却颇具先锋和前瞻性的《四季》之后，关于如何演奏维瓦尔第音乐的论题便被音乐节拿出来进行反复讨论和实验。在德·斯瓦特本次带来的版本中，他放大了维瓦尔第用音乐编码自然之声的元素，着重强调了小提琴歌唱般的旋律线条，而更亮眼的是他的乐团伴奏，尤其是承担了推动曲目情景发展的同奏低音，在处理重复音符时动态感十足，不再是作为普通的框架支撑，而是填满了和谐自然的装饰音的充满血肉的土壤，与盘旋于上的独奏小提琴之间形成了完美的互动。尤其是在《春》的第三乐章和《秋》的第一乐章这两节中，两者之间的对话场景令人想起了莫扎特的《魔笛》中的吹笛人与鸟，有来有往互通款曲——酒神狂欢并不是一人的庆典，独奏自然流畅，没有多余的夸张装饰，反倒是同奏低音奔涌前进，极具立体感。

这也非常符合18世纪时的审美美学。受启蒙思想的影响，18世纪的艺术家们普遍通过模仿自然来探讨理性、美学与和谐之间的关系。

歌德在

《歌德谈话录

（

Gespräche mit Goethe

）》

中提到，

艺术家与自然之间存在双重关系：他既是自然的主宰，又是自然的奴隶。在今晚的演出中，不同声部之间对于自然之声的模仿既出自于18世纪作曲家谱曲时对于不同场景做出的精准指示，同时也是21世纪的年轻艺术家对这一概念做出的新的解读，可以用康德的一句话来概括：

“艺术是自然的模拟，但它是通过自由的目的性而创造的。”

（Die Kunst ahmt die Natur nach, aber sie ist durch freie Zweckmäßigkeit geschaffen.）

德·斯瓦特和Le

Consort在他们的演奏中将他们的想法（意志）和审美判断为基石，原本只是充当骨架结构的同奏低音经过他们的重新思考塑造变成了丰饶的森林，令人不禁想起了波提切利的《春》的场景。

独奏和伴奏之间的频繁互动让这部早就被演烂了的曲目重现生机，音乐家之间的呼吸步调一致，16人的团体却演出了四重中一般的亲密感。感谢听众对于曲目的熟悉，使得曲目中的种种元素变得极易识别，因此，当独奏和伴奏之间做出一些“出格”的动态对比或在旋律中增加更多的歌唱性时，在聆听音乐之余，辨识这些元素的变化乐趣也为演出增加了不少趣味性，台上台下的互动在这一刻也成为了非刻意的、自然的行为。

散场之后和德·斯瓦特聊了几句，谈及我对他出道那年录的普鲁斯特时代的音乐的喜爱，我说，我曾经一度非常喜爱在夜晚听着你的这张专辑在街上散步，他哈哈大笑，说，那你一定找到了最普鲁斯特的感觉。

另外有意思的是，因为本场演出几乎一票难求，我在最后刷到了一张退票，没想到意外发现了一个新天地。在爱乐小厅的二楼有一排非常幽谧的座位，灯光幽谧没有人来人往和邻座纷扰，找个舒服的姿势安安静静听一整场，对于台上互动细节的辨识变得更敏锐，也更能寻找到他们在装饰音变化中做出的微小调整，从而丰容自己的演出体验。

可惜下半场暖气跟不上了，冷得我灵魂出窍
translations.en:
Paris has plunged into a sudden cold these past days; every morning when I look out the window I can see a white frost laid over the park lawn below, worse after sunset. Walking toward the Philharmonie, cold gusts hit me, and because the Paris government has switched streetlights to LEDs for environmental reasons, the whole street is pitch-black except for small circular pools of light beneath the lamps. The park at the Philharmonie’s entrance is so dark that even the silhouettes of the plants become blurred, inevitably evoking the French winters depicted by George Sand: darkness devours everything, and the cold night wind howls through the trees. The red corridor of the Cité de la musique stands at the end of that darkness; beyond the corridor is the concert hall with its heating turned up full blast.

Tonight’s performance was given by France’s gifted Baroque violin rising star Théotime Langlois de Swarte and his ensemble Le Consort, presenting works by Vivaldi and Giovanni Legrenzi. Like many excellent contemporary French early-music musicians, de Swarte came out of William Christie’s Les Arts Florissants. The violin he used tonight is the Jacob Steiner instrument made in 1665 that he has used frequently on recordings, and his bow was made by Pierre Tourte.

It’s hard to imagine that someone born in 1995 could perform at this level.

The concert opened with an aria from Legrenzi’s opera La divisione del mondo; the contrapuntal writing is gentle and serene, and de Swarte’s playing traced long, singing lines. As one of Vivaldi’s teachers, Legrenzi made decisive contributions to music’s development: he was the first composer to adopt a three-movement sonata structure—a form that later solidified and became widely used. Even Bach in Leipzig was deeply influenced by him and composed a fugue on his theme, BWV 574.

The centerpiece of the evening was Vivaldi’s Four Seasons. Before performing the Spring movement, de Swarte offered a brief introduction: this repertoire has been played so often it’s known to passersby, so he would say little and only asked the audience to listen to his re-orchestrated version—which is also the content of the new album he was releasing tomorrow (January 17).

Since Nikolaus Harnoncourt’s controversial but now forward-looking 1977 edition of The Four Seasons, debates and experiments about how to perform Vivaldi have repeatedly surfaced at festivals. In de Swarte’s version, he enlarges Vivaldi’s musical coding of natural sounds, emphasizing the violin’s singing melodic line. More striking is his ensemble’s accompaniment, particularly the ripieno basso continuo that drives the dramatic scenes. When handling repeated notes, it displays vivid dynamics; it is no longer merely a structural frame but becomes a flesh-and-blood earth filled with harmonically natural decorative tones, creating a perfect interplay with the soaring solo violin. Especially in the third movement of Spring and the first movement of Autumn, the dialogue between the two calls to mind the exchanges between the Piper and the Birds in Mozart’s The Magic Flute—reciprocal, conversational. The Bacchanalian revel is not a solitary celebration: the solo is naturally fluent, without excessive ornamentation, while the ripieno basso rushes forward with tremendous three-dimensionality.

This approach also aligns well with eighteenth-century aesthetic sensibilities. Influenced by Enlightenment thought, eighteenth-century artists commonly explored the relationships among reason, aesthetics, and harmony through imitation of nature.

Goethe, in Conversations with Goethe (Gespräche mit Goethe), mentioned that artists have a dual relationship with nature: they are both masters of nature and its slaves. In tonight’s performance, the imitation of natural sounds across different parts stems both from the eighteenth-century composers’ precise indications for various scenes and from twenty-first-century young artists’ new interpretations of that concept. It can be summed up with a line from Kant: “Art imitates nature, but it is created through free purposiveness.” (Die Kunst ahmt die Natur nach, aber sie ist durch freie Zweckmäßigkeit geschaffen.)

De Swarte and Le Consort based their performance on their intentions and aesthetic judgments; what was originally just a skeletal continuo was reshaped by their rethinking into a fertile forest, evoking Botticelli’s Primavera.

Frequent interaction between soloist and accompaniment brought fresh life to a piece that has long been played to exhaustion: the musicians breathed together, and the sixteen-member group produced an intimacy more like that of a quartet. Thanks to the audience’s familiarity with the repertoire, the piece’s elements became instantly recognizable; when soloist and ensemble made some “out-of-the-ordinary” dynamic contrasts or added greater lyricism to a melody, the pleasure of identifying those changes while listening added considerable interest to the performance. The interaction between stage and audience at that moment felt unforced and natural.

After the concert I chatted a bit with de Swarte. I mentioned my fondness for the Proust-era music he recorded the year he debuted and said I used to love walking the streets at night listening to that album. He laughed heartily and said, “Then you must have found the most Proustian feeling.”

Another amusing detail: because tonight’s concert was nearly sold out, I unexpectedly scored a returned ticket at the last minute and discovered a new paradise. On the second floor of the small Philharmonie hall there is a row of extremely serene seats—soft lighting, no comings and goings, no neighborly disturbances. Finding a comfortable position and quietly listening to an entire concert there made me much more sensitive to the stage’s interactive details; I could more readily pick up the tiny adjustments they made in decorative figures and thereby enrich my concert experience.

Unfortunately, the heating couldn’t keep up in the second half; it was so cold I felt my soul leave my body.
translations.es:
Hace unos días, la temperatura en París cayó en picado; cada mañana al asomarme por la ventana veía una capa de escarcha en el césped del parque de abajo, más evidente aún después de que el sol se hubiera puesto. Caminando hacia la sala de la Filarmónica hacía un frío cortante; además, el gobierno parisino, por motivos ecológicos, había reemplazado las farolas por iluminación LED, de modo que, salvo por aquella pequeña mancha circular de luz bajo cada farol, la calle quedaba sumida en la oscuridad. El parque frente al edificio de la Filarmónica estaba tan oscuro que incluso las siluetas de las plantas se volvían indistintas, evocando el invierno francés de George Sand: la noche devora todo y el viento helado aúlla entre los árboles. El corredor rojo de la antigua Cité de la musique se alzaba al fondo de esa oscuridad; al atravesarlo se entraba en una sala calefaccionada y cálida.

La velada estuvo protagonizada por la joven promesa barroca francesa Théotime Langlois de Swarte y su conjunto Le Consort, quienes interpretaron obras de Vivaldi y de Giovanni Legrenzi. Al igual que muchos excelentes músicos barrocos contemporáneos en Francia, De Swarte proviene de la órbita de William Christie, fundador de Les Arts Florissants. El violín que utilizó para este concierto, el mismo que emplea en varias grabaciones, fue fabricado por Jacob Steiner en 1665, y el arco era obra de Pierre Tourte.

Es difícil imaginar que alguien nacido en 1995 pueda tocar a tal nivel.

El concierto se abrió con un aria de la ópera de Legrenzi La divisione del mondo; era una pieza contrapuntística, suave y serena, y la línea de De Swarte sonó larga y cantabile. Legrenzi, uno de los maestros de Vivaldi, tuvo una influencia decisiva en el desarrollo musical: fue pionero en el empleo de la forma de sonata en tres movimientos, una estructura que más tarde se consolidaría y difundiría ampliamente. Incluso Bach, lejos en Leipzig, se sintió influido por él y compuso una fuga temática BWV 574 en relación con esa influencia.

La pieza central de la noche fue Las cuatro estaciones de Vivaldi. Antes del movimiento “Primavera”, De Swarte hizo una breve introducción: explicó que el ciclo está tan sobejamente conocido que no haría una larga presentación, y sólo pidió a la audiencia que escuchara su versión reorquestada —la que aparece en su nuevo álbum, que saldría mañana, 17 de enero.

Desde que Nikolaus Harnoncourt propuso en 1977 una edición de Las cuatro estaciones que entonces fue muy controvertida y que hoy resulta previsora y vanguardista, la cuestión de cómo interpretar la música de Vivaldi ha sido objeto de reiteradas discusiones y experimentos en los festivales. En la versión que presentó De Swarte amplificó los elementos con los que Vivaldi codificó los sonidos de la naturaleza, priorizando la línea melódica del violín como canto. Más llamativo aún fue el papel de la acompañamiento: el bajo continuo no se limitó a ofrecer un armazón, sino que, en su tratamiento de las notas repetidas, desplegó una dinámica llena de vida, convirtiéndose en un suelo fecundo y cargado de decoraciones armónicas que interactuaron perfectamente con el violín solista. En particular, en el tercer movimiento de “Primavera” y en el primer movimiento de “Otoño”, ese diálogo recordó la relación entre el flautista y los pájaros en La flauta mágica de Mozart: un intercambio recíproco y comunicativo —el jolgorio bacanal no es celebración de uno solo—. El solista fluyó con naturalidad, sin adornos excesivos, mientras el bajo continuo avanzaba desbordante, dando una sensación muy tridimensional.

Esta lectura encaja bien con la estética del siglo XVIII. Bajo la influencia de la Ilustración, los artistas de ese siglo solían explorar la relación entre la razón, la estética y la armonía a través de la imitación de la naturaleza. Goethe, en Gespräche mit Goethe, observó que la relación del artista con la naturaleza es doble: el artista es a la vez amo y siervo de la naturaleza. En la actuación de esta noche, la imitación de los sonidos naturales por parte de las distintas voces no sólo obedecía a las precisas indicaciones que los compositores del XVIII plasmaron en sus partituras, sino que también representaba una nueva interpretación del concepto por parte de jóvenes artistas del siglo XXI. Como lo sintetiza una frase de Kant: “Die Kunst ahmt die Natur nach, aber sie ist durch freie Zweckmäßigkeit geschaffen.” (El arte imita la naturaleza, pero se crea mediante una finalidad libre.)

De Swarte y Le Consort cimentaron su lectura en su voluntad y en juicios estéticos propios: el bajo continuo, originalmente concebido como simple estructura esquelética, fue repensado y modelado hasta convertirse en un bosque fecundo que evocaba la escena de La Primavera de Botticelli.

La frecuente interacción entre solista y acompañamiento insufló vida a una obra ya muy interpretada; los músicos respiraban al unísono y, pese a ser un conjunto de dieciséis intérpretes, lograron una intimidad similar a la de un cuarteto. La familiaridad del público con el repertorio facilitó el reconocimiento de los distintos elementos musicales, de modo que cuando el solista y la orquesta introducían contrastes dinámicos “fuera de lo esperado” o añadían mayor cantabilidad a la melodía, identificar esas variaciones resultaba un placer que añadió gusto al concierto. En ese instante, la interacción entre escenario y sala se volvió natural y no buscada.

Al finalizar salí y conversé brevemente con De Swarte. Le comenté cuánto me había gustado la música de la época proustiana que grabó en su año de debut: le conté que durante una etapa solía escuchar ese disco por la noche mientras paseaba por las calles. Se rió a carcajadas y dijo: “Entonces debiste haber encontrado la sensación más proustiana.”

Otro detalle curioso: como las entradas para esta función estaban prácticamente agotadas, conseguí por suerte una devolución de última hora y descubrí un pequeño paraíso. En la planta alta de la sala pequeña de la Filarmónica hay una fila de asientos muy tranquilos, con una iluminación suave, sin idas y venidas ni ruidos de los asientos contiguos. Encontrar una postura cómoda y escuchar la función en silencio permite detectar con mayor agudeza los detalles de la interacción y las mínimas variaciones en los adornos, lo que enriquece la experiencia.

Lástima que en la segunda parte la calefacción no rindiera; hacía tanto frío que sentí como si mi alma saliera del cuerpo.

contents.en:
Paris has plunged into a sudden cold these past days; every morning when I look out the window I can see a white frost laid over the park lawn below, worse after sunset. Walking toward the Philharmonie, cold gusts hit me, and because the Paris government has switched streetlights to LEDs for environmental reasons, the whole street is pitch-black except for small circular pools of light beneath the lamps. The park at the Philharmonie’s entrance is so dark that even the silhouettes of the plants become blurred, inevitably evoking the French winters depicted by George Sand: darkness devours everything, and the cold night wind howls through the trees. The red corridor of the Cité de la musique stands at the end of that darkness; beyond the corridor is the concert hall with its heating turned up full blast.

Tonight’s performance was given by France’s gifted Baroque violin rising star Théotime Langlois de Swarte and his ensemble Le Consort, presenting works by Vivaldi and Giovanni Legrenzi. Like many excellent contemporary French early-music musicians, de Swarte came out of William Christie’s Les Arts Florissants. The violin he used tonight is the Jacob Steiner instrument made in 1665 that he has used frequently on recordings, and his bow was made by Pierre Tourte.

It’s hard to imagine that someone born in 1995 could perform at this level.

The concert opened with an aria from Legrenzi’s opera La divisione del mondo; the contrapuntal writing is gentle and serene, and de Swarte’s playing traced long, singing lines. As one of Vivaldi’s teachers, Legrenzi made decisive contributions to music’s development: he was the first composer to adopt a three-movement sonata structure—a form that later solidified and became widely used. Even Bach in Leipzig was deeply influenced by him and composed a fugue on his theme, BWV 574.

The centerpiece of the evening was Vivaldi’s Four Seasons. Before performing the Spring movement, de Swarte offered a brief introduction: this repertoire has been played so often it’s known to passersby, so he would say little and only asked the audience to listen to his re-orchestrated version—which is also the content of the new album he was releasing tomorrow (January 17).

Since Nikolaus Harnoncourt’s controversial but now forward-looking 1977 edition of The Four Seasons, debates and experiments about how to perform Vivaldi have repeatedly surfaced at festivals. In de Swarte’s version, he enlarges Vivaldi’s musical coding of natural sounds, emphasizing the violin’s singing melodic line. More striking is his ensemble’s accompaniment, particularly the ripieno basso continuo that drives the dramatic scenes. When handling repeated notes, it displays vivid dynamics; it is no longer merely a structural frame but becomes a flesh-and-blood earth filled with harmonically natural decorative tones, creating a perfect interplay with the soaring solo violin. Especially in the third movement of Spring and the first movement of Autumn, the dialogue between the two calls to mind the exchanges between the Piper and the Birds in Mozart’s The Magic Flute—reciprocal, conversational. The Bacchanalian revel is not a solitary celebration: the solo is naturally fluent, without excessive ornamentation, while the ripieno basso rushes forward with tremendous three-dimensionality.

This approach also aligns well with eighteenth-century aesthetic sensibilities. Influenced by Enlightenment thought, eighteenth-century artists commonly explored the relationships among reason, aesthetics, and harmony through imitation of nature.

Goethe, in Conversations with Goethe (Gespräche mit Goethe), mentioned that artists have a dual relationship with nature: they are both masters of nature and its slaves. In tonight’s performance, the imitation of natural sounds across different parts stems both from the eighteenth-century composers’ precise indications for various scenes and from twenty-first-century young artists’ new interpretations of that concept. It can be summed up with a line from Kant: “Art imitates nature, but it is created through free purposiveness.” (Die Kunst ahmt die Natur nach, aber sie ist durch freie Zweckmäßigkeit geschaffen.)

De Swarte and Le Consort based their performance on their intentions and aesthetic judgments; what was originally just a skeletal continuo was reshaped by their rethinking into a fertile forest, evoking Botticelli’s Primavera.

Frequent interaction between soloist and accompaniment brought fresh life to a piece that has long been played to exhaustion: the musicians breathed together, and the sixteen-member group produced an intimacy more like that of a quartet. Thanks to the audience’s familiarity with the repertoire, the piece’s elements became instantly recognizable; when soloist and ensemble made some “out-of-the-ordinary” dynamic contrasts or added greater lyricism to a melody, the pleasure of identifying those changes while listening added considerable interest to the performance. The interaction between stage and audience at that moment felt unforced and natural.

After the concert I chatted a bit with de Swarte. I mentioned my fondness for the Proust-era music he recorded the year he debuted and said I used to love walking the streets at night listening to that album. He laughed heartily and said, “Then you must have found the most Proustian feeling.”

Another amusing detail: because tonight’s concert was nearly sold out, I unexpectedly scored a returned ticket at the last minute and discovered a new paradise. On the second floor of the small Philharmonie hall there is a row of extremely serene seats—soft lighting, no comings and goings, no neighborly disturbances. Finding a comfortable position and quietly listening to an entire concert there made me much more sensitive to the stage’s interactive details; I could more readily pick up the tiny adjustments they made in decorative figures and thereby enrich my concert experience.

Unfortunately, the heating couldn’t keep up in the second half; it was so cold I felt my soul leave my body.

Hace unos días, la temperatura en París cayó en picado; cada mañana al asomarme por la ventana veía una capa de escarcha en el césped del parque de abajo, más evidente aún después de que el sol se hubiera puesto. Caminando hacia la sala de la Filarmónica hacía un frío cortante; además, el gobierno parisino, por motivos ecológicos, había reemplazado las farolas por iluminación LED, de modo que, salvo por aquella pequeña mancha circular de luz bajo cada farol, la calle quedaba sumida en la oscuridad. El parque frente al edificio de la Filarmónica estaba tan oscuro que incluso las siluetas de las plantas se volvían indistintas, evocando el invierno francés de George Sand: la noche devora todo y el viento helado aúlla entre los árboles. El corredor rojo de la antigua Cité de la musique se alzaba al fondo de esa oscuridad; al atravesarlo se entraba en una sala calefaccionada y cálida.

La velada estuvo protagonizada por la joven promesa barroca francesa Théotime Langlois de Swarte y su conjunto Le Consort, quienes interpretaron obras de Vivaldi y de Giovanni Legrenzi. Al igual que muchos excelentes músicos barrocos contemporáneos en Francia, De Swarte proviene de la órbita de William Christie, fundador de Les Arts Florissants. El violín que utilizó para este concierto, el mismo que emplea en varias grabaciones, fue fabricado por Jacob Steiner en 1665, y el arco era obra de Pierre Tourte.

Es difícil imaginar que alguien nacido en 1995 pueda tocar a tal nivel.

El concierto se abrió con un aria de la ópera de Legrenzi La divisione del mondo; era una pieza contrapuntística, suave y serena, y la línea de De Swarte sonó larga y cantabile. Legrenzi, uno de los maestros de Vivaldi, tuvo una influencia decisiva en el desarrollo musical: fue pionero en el empleo de la forma de sonata en tres movimientos, una estructura que más tarde se consolidaría y difundiría ampliamente. Incluso Bach, lejos en Leipzig, se sintió influido por él y compuso una fuga temática BWV 574 en relación con esa influencia.

La pieza central de la noche fue Las cuatro estaciones de Vivaldi. Antes del movimiento “Primavera”, De Swarte hizo una breve introducción: explicó que el ciclo está tan sobejamente conocido que no haría una larga presentación, y sólo pidió a la audiencia que escuchara su versión reorquestada —la que aparece en su nuevo álbum, que saldría mañana, 17 de enero.

Desde que Nikolaus Harnoncourt propuso en 1977 una edición de Las cuatro estaciones que entonces fue muy controvertida y que hoy resulta previsora y vanguardista, la cuestión de cómo interpretar la música de Vivaldi ha sido objeto de reiteradas discusiones y experimentos en los festivales. En la versión que presentó De Swarte amplificó los elementos con los que Vivaldi codificó los sonidos de la naturaleza, priorizando la línea melódica del violín como canto. Más llamativo aún fue el papel de la acompañamiento: el bajo continuo no se limitó a ofrecer un armazón, sino que, en su tratamiento de las notas repetidas, desplegó una dinámica llena de vida, convirtiéndose en un suelo fecundo y cargado de decoraciones armónicas que interactuaron perfectamente con el violín solista. En particular, en el tercer movimiento de “Primavera” y en el primer movimiento de “Otoño”, ese diálogo recordó la relación entre el flautista y los pájaros en La flauta mágica de Mozart: un intercambio recíproco y comunicativo —el jolgorio bacanal no es celebración de uno solo—. El solista fluyó con naturalidad, sin adornos excesivos, mientras el bajo continuo avanzaba desbordante, dando una sensación muy tridimensional.

Esta lectura encaja bien con la estética del siglo XVIII. Bajo la influencia de la Ilustración, los artistas de ese siglo solían explorar la relación entre la razón, la estética y la armonía a través de la imitación de la naturaleza. Goethe, en Gespräche mit Goethe, observó que la relación del artista con la naturaleza es doble: el artista es a la vez amo y siervo de la naturaleza. En la actuación de esta noche, la imitación de los sonidos naturales por parte de las distintas voces no sólo obedecía a las precisas indicaciones que los compositores del XVIII plasmaron en sus partituras, sino que también representaba una nueva interpretación del concepto por parte de jóvenes artistas del siglo XXI. Como lo sintetiza una frase de Kant: “Die Kunst ahmt die Natur nach, aber sie ist durch freie Zweckmäßigkeit geschaffen.” (El arte imita la naturaleza, pero se crea mediante una finalidad libre.)

De Swarte y Le Consort cimentaron su lectura en su voluntad y en juicios estéticos propios: el bajo continuo, originalmente concebido como simple estructura esquelética, fue repensado y modelado hasta convertirse en un bosque fecundo que evocaba la escena de La Primavera de Botticelli.

La frecuente interacción entre solista y acompañamiento insufló vida a una obra ya muy interpretada; los músicos respiraban al unísono y, pese a ser un conjunto de dieciséis intérpretes, lograron una intimidad similar a la de un cuarteto. La familiaridad del público con el repertorio facilitó el reconocimiento de los distintos elementos musicales, de modo que cuando el solista y la orquesta introducían contrastes dinámicos “fuera de lo esperado” o añadían mayor cantabilidad a la melodía, identificar esas variaciones resultaba un placer que añadió gusto al concierto. En ese instante, la interacción entre escenario y sala se volvió natural y no buscada.

Al finalizar salí y conversé brevemente con De Swarte. Le comenté cuánto me había gustado la música de la época proustiana que grabó en su año de debut: le conté que durante una etapa solía escuchar ese disco por la noche mientras paseaba por las calles. Se rió a carcajadas y dijo: “Entonces debiste haber encontrado la sensación más proustiana.”

Otro detalle curioso: como las entradas para esta función estaban prácticamente agotadas, conseguí por suerte una devolución de última hora y descubrí un pequeño paraíso. En la planta alta de la sala pequeña de la Filarmónica hay una fila de asientos muy tranquilos, con una iluminación suave, sin idas y venidas ni ruidos de los asientos contiguos. Encontrar una postura cómoda y escuchar la función en silencio permite detectar con mayor agudeza los detalles de la interacción y las mínimas variaciones en los adornos, lo que enriquece la experiencia.

Lástima que en la segunda parte la calefacción no rindiera; hacía tanto frío que sentí como si mi alma saliera del cuerpo.

contents.en: The French repertoire still holds many forgotten treasures. The Estivales de Puisaye will demonstrate this from August 13 to 16 by reviving Giroflé-Girofla, one of Charles Lecocq’s greatest successes. Created in 1874, the opéra-bouffe enjoyed success on European and American stages before falling into obscurity: no professional production has been staged in France since Angers in 2016, and the work has yet to receive a first recording. Philippe Brocard, serving as both conductor and director, offers a chamber version for quartet and piano faithful to the score’s sparkling spirit; sets and costumes are by Cléo Ben Lahcène. articles.title: 再版：Pascal Rogé — Complete Decca Recordings
articles.result: Decca 为钢琴家 Pascal Rogé 的七十五岁生日推出再版盒装《Pascal Rogé. Complete Decca Recordings》。Rogé 自1968年起与 Decca 合作——在朱利叶斯·卡钦（Julius Katchen）的引荐下签下一份为期六年的合约，后来在该厂长达整整三十年。此次43张CD的套装在原有遗产基础上加入若干未发行录音，并借用部分后期为 Onyx 与 ASV 所录（如补全的德彪西全集、与 Raymond Leppard 合作的两首莫扎特协奏曲及完整的弗朗克专辑）。法兰西曲目占比最大：德彪西的《图像》（1977）与《前奏曲》被称为质地深厚、节奏迷人；拉威尔的《镜子》（1974）有细腻但录音偏硬的特点；与 Charles Dutoit 合作的协奏曲（八年后录音）被评价为令人失望。Rogé 的萨蒂以细致 rubato 吸引，1996年与 Jean‑Philippe Collard 的四手联弹表现出色；他与 Pierre Amoyal 及 Quatuor Ysaÿe 的福雷作品同样成功。Rogé 的代表性工程为1986–1998年间完成的普朗克全集（共11张CD，含协奏曲、室内乐与歌曲，合作歌手包括 Catherine Dubosc、Gilles Cachemaille、Felicity Lott 与 François Le Roux），展示了他的品味与受控的热情。套装亦收录圣-桑五部协奏曲、罕见的 d’Indy、Roussel、Tansman、Françaix（《牧羊人的时刻》）与 Milhaud 的作品，并收有1976年与 Lorin Maazel 在克利夫兰的弗朗克《交响变奏曲》。此外他涉猎布拉姆斯、李斯特、巴托克等曲目（如1991年与 Pierre Amoyal 合作的三部奏鸣曲，1974–1976年与 Walter Weller 及伦敦交响乐团录制的巴托克三协奏曲等），展现清晰、优雅与可靠的技术。该套装由 Decca 出品，43 CD，获 Cinq Diapason 评价。

contents.en: Decca has issued a reissue box set, "Pascal Rogé. Complete Decca Recordings," to mark Pascal Rogé’s seventy‑fifth birthday. Rogé’s relationship with Decca began in 1968: thanks to Julius Katchen he signed a six‑year contract and ultimately remained with the label for exactly three decades. The 43‑CD set supplements the label’s legacy with a handful of previously unreleased items and borrows some later recordings issued on Onyx and ASV (notably to complete the Debussy set and to include two Mozart concertos with Raymond Leppard, as well as a full Franck album). French repertoire predominates: highlights include Debussy’s Images (1977) and Preludes noted for their inhabited density and slow allure; Ravel’s Miroirs (1974) is delicate though the sound is described as hard; the concertos with Charles Dutoit recorded eight years later are judged disappointing. Rogé’s Satie, characterized by fine rubato, and his four‑hand pieces with Jean‑Philippe Collard (1996) are praised; his Fauré recordings, including collaborations with Pierre Amoyal and the Quatuor Ysaÿe, are successful. His major achievement for the label is the complete Poulenc (1986–1998), eleven CDs covering concertante works, chamber music and mélodies with Catherine Dubosc, Gilles Cachemaille, Felicity Lott and François Le Roux, showing his taste and controlled verve. The set also includes the five Saint‑Saëns concertos with Charles Dutoit, rare works by d’Indy, Roussel, Tansman, Françaix (L’Heure du berger) and Milhaud (Sonate op.47) with leading French wind players, and Franck’s Variations symphoniques with Lorin Maazel in Cleveland (1976). Rogé’s ventures into other repertoire—Brahms sonatas with Pierre Amoyal (1991), Liszt recordings (1969 and later), the Pleiades Dances by Takashi Yoshimatsu (1998) and Bartók’s three concertos with Walter Weller and the London Symphony (1974–1976)—demonstrate clarity, elegance and technical reliability. The box is released by Decca (43 CDs) and is noted as Cinq Diapason.

articles.title: 瓦格纳：《莱茵的黄金》——拜罗伊特
articles.result: 在拜罗伊特音乐节庆祝成立150周年之际，上演了以“Ring 10010110”（二进制150）、副题《Vom Mythos zum Code》为名的《莱茵的黄金》。本制作由Roman Senkl负责概念与人工智能合成，Marcus Lobbes指导AI选择与改编，布景Wolf Gutjahr，服装Pia Maria Mackert，拜罗伊特音乐节管弦乐团由Christian Thielemann指挥。节目背景为今年安排三套《尼伯龙根的指环》循环，本次报道观看的是第二个循环；节庆筹划曾遭遇原先宏大名单缩减（Lohengrin、Tannhäuser、Tristan und Isolde被删）、财政困难及围绕一场被取消后临时重排的关于音乐节历史性反犹问题的会议的争议，但演出票自2026年3月起即告售罄。舞台以一块几乎看不见的透明幕布投射快速、变形的图像为主，AI合成的16部历史制作片段以极快节奏出现，评论指出这些投影常使人物被遮蔽并削弱表演动线，服装为十四位主要演员设计的近似羽毛的灰色连体装，Loge由Klaus-Florian Vogt饰演并配有天使翅膀。尽管舞台概念遭批评，音乐与声乐受到高度评价：Michael Volle首度在拜罗伊特饰演Wotan，声音被评为宏阔；Anna Kissjudit的Fricka、Jochen Schmeckenbecher的Alberich及三位莱茵女儿Katharina Konradi、Natalia Skrycka与Marie-Henriette Reinhold等演出获赞。观众在开场时对技术团队出现曾有嘘声，本剧第一幕开始后嘘声被对歌唱者的热烈喝彩取代；Christian Thielemann同样获得极大掌声并被视为此地的重要指挥人物。

contents.en: Staged for Bayreuth’s 150th-anniversary season, the production titled “Ring 10010110” (150 in binary) with the subtitle “Vom Mythos zum Code” presents Das Rheingold using an AI-based concept. Roman Senkl is credited for conception and artificial intelligence work, Marcus Lobbes guided the AI selection and adaptation, sets are by Wolf Gutjahr, costumes by Pia Maria Mackert, and the Bayreuth Festival Orchestra is conducted by Christian Thielemann. The festival programmed three Ring cycles this year; the report covers the second cycle. The anniversary edition faced earlier setbacks: an initially vast program was reduced (Lohengrin, Tannhäuser and Tristan und Isolde were dropped), the festival’s finances were described as moribund, and a controversy arose over a cancelled then reprogrammed conference addressing systemic antisemitism in the festival’s history; nevertheless all tickets had been sold out since March 2026. The staging relies on a nearly invisible transparent screen onto which rapid, kaleidoscopic images—an AI synthesis of sixteen past Ring productions—are projected; reviewers note the images often obscure and make performers invisible, and reduce dramatic action, while costumes for the fourteen principals are similar grey, feather-like suits, Loge (Klaus-Florian Vogt) being given angel wings. Musically the performance was praised: Michael Volle made his Bayreuth debut as Wotan with an ample voice; Anna Kissjudit (Fricka), Jochen Schmeckenbecher (Alberich) and the Rhine maidens Katharina Konradi, Natalia Skrycka and Marie-Henriette Reinhold received positive mention. Audience reaction included loud boos when the technical team appeared at bows in a prior event, and at this performance initial jeers gave way to strong acclaim for the singers; Christian Thielemann received enthusiastic salutes and was singled out for his leadership.

articles.title: Sonya Yoncheva 与 Domingo Hindoyan 首次夫妻同台录音！
articles.result: 索尼娅·约恩切娃（Sonya Yoncheva，女高音）与指挥丈夫 Domingo Hindoyan 携手，与皇家利物浦爱乐管弦乐团推出首张夫妻共演专辑，随 Onyx 唱片出品（Onyx (D) ONYX4274S，日文解说附带的进口盘），含税定价为￥3,470。该专辑是约恩切娃在 Onyx 旗下的首次登场，节目单选用较为出人意料的马尔图奇（Martucci）与康特卢布（Canteloube）作品，而非她惯常的意大利歌剧或巴洛克曲目。约恩切娃演唱马尔图奇的两首作品《回想の歌》与《夜想曲》，其丰富的连奏与长句所展现的抒情性与她的声音和表现力相得益彰。康特卢布方面收录其1914年完成的《トリプティーク》（三曲组成的歌曲集），以颂扬自然的诗为词，管弦乐色彩与声乐融为一体；另有交响诗《遠き姫君へ》，此曲为首次世界录音。资料同时指出，约恩切娃自2010年在普拉西ド·多明戈创立的国际声乐比赛“Operalia”获奖后迅速成名，常在大都会歌剧院、皇家歌剧院、米兰斯卡拉、维也纳国立歌剧院、柏林国立歌剧院与巴黎歌剧院等顶级舞台担任主演。2023年她也曾以拿手剧目《托斯卡》在日本完成令人瞩目的歌剧首演。

articles.title: 权力示威？——瓦格纳屋里的克里斯蒂安
articles.result: 作者回顾了Christian Thielemanns在拜罗伊特的一场《瓦尔基里》演出，并围绕Markus Thiel将Thielemanns《莱茵金》称为“Machtdemonstration”（权力示威）的说法展开讨论。文章具体描述了Thielemann在瓦格纳音乐中对大段落的处理：用长波形构建瓦坦的告别，强调大调与小调间的微妙平衡、让大调和弦望入雷鸣般的小调之渊、延迟和充分发挥半音预备音与解決，缓慢堆积属音张力以反复挫败听众期待然后赐予调性宁静，擅长将苦难与渴望戏剧化。独唱方面，Camilla Nylund与Michael Volle全然追随指挥并呈现出色戏剧效果；Elza van den Heever的Sieglinde偏尖厉，Klaus Florian Vogt的Siegmund近似Siegfried的气质。文中还以“瓦格纳屋”比喻Thielemann三十年打造的个人瓦格纳诠释体系：他熟知每一处细节，有时显得自得甚至略感乏味、爱以低调或挑衅的方式示人。作者指出，其他指挥如Kirill Petrenko（萨尔茨堡）、Pablo Heras-Casado、Simone Young、Vladimir Jurowski与Antonio Pappano等，正从外部视角为瓦格纳带来新鲜气息：Petrenko强调乐谱的垂直深度，Heras‑Casado着重色彩，Young注重戏剧化。结论是：Thielemann的演绎固然成熟，但在他自己的“瓦格纳屋”里似乎有些无聊，或该开窗透透气。作者为Axel Brüggemann，并列举了其作为作者、导演和媒体人的工作经历与出版、获奖记录（文章原文说明）。

contents.en: The article reviews Christian Thielemann’s Ring-related work at Bayreuth and reflects on Markus Thiel’s description of Thielemann’s Rheingold as a “Machtdemonstration” (show of power). It analyzes how Thielemann shaped the Walküre — notably Wotan’s farewell — with long-wave phrasing, an extreme balance between major and minor, letting major chords peer into thunderous minor, savoring chromatic suspensions and delayed resolutions, and building dominant tensions almost unbearably slowly to frustrate audience expectations before granting tonal rest. Thielemann is portrayed as a master at staging suffering and longing. Soloists Camilla Nylund and Michael Volle are said to follow him uncompromisingly and deliver a perfect drama; Elza van den Heever’s Sieglinde is described as rather strident, and Klaus Florian Vogt’s Siegmund as Siegfried-like. The author uses the metaphor of Thielemann’s “Wagner house” — a Wagner interpretation he has furnished over thirty years, knowing every detail — and suggests he sometimes appears bored, showy or deliberately understated. Other conductors such as Kirill Petrenko (Salzburg), Pablo Heras‑Casado, Simone Young, Vladimir Jurowski and Antonio Pappano are cited as bringing fresh external perspectives: Petrenko emphasized vertical depth of the score, Heras‑Casado explored color, Young focused on drama. The piece concludes that while Thielemann’s approach is coherent and authoritative, it can feel a bit settled or inward-looking, and perhaps it is time to “air out” his Wagner. The article is by Axel Brüggemann, with biographical notes on his work as an author, director and broadcaster and his publications and awards (as given in the original).

articles.title: 圣塞巴斯蒂安 / 弗洛雷斯在 Quincena Musical Donostiarra 开幕音乐会上的慷慨表现
articles.result: 昆西纳·多诺斯蒂亚拉音乐节（Quincena Musical Donostiarra）第八十七届于2026年8月2日在奥迪托里奥·库尔萨尔开幕，秘鲁男高音Juan Diego Flórez与其常任钢琴伴奏Vincenzo Scalera献唱，门票早已售罄。尽管歌唱家当日因喉部不适而在台上使用纸巾、吸入器及一杯“神秘药剂”，他仍决定维持演出并对节目做出小幅删节与一次换曲以保护上声区。上半场以贝里尼的三首歌曲、两段罗西尼小咏叹调及多尼采蒂的“Oh! Rammenta, bella Irene”为主；原计划的《La Cenerentola》一段被改为罗西尼《La pietra del paragone》中的咏叹调以避免超高音。下半场以西班牙与法国曲目为主，含Soutullo y Vert、Pérez Soriano、Serrano的曲目，Scalera演奏了Lecuona的Mazurka“Glissando”，随后Flórez演唱了Massenet的“Pourquoi me réveiller?”与Gounod的“Ah, lève-toi, soleil”，在Gounod曲目中完成了文中所称的“三个不可避免的si sobreagudos”。Scalera的伴奏和数次独奏（包括罗西尼片段、Lecuona与Godard作品）获得高度赞赏。安可环节Flórez以吉他演唱多首流行与民谣（包括Gardel的《Volver》、《La flor de la canela》、《Fina estampa》和《Cucurrucucú, paloma》），最终由Scalera以Leoncavallo的《Mattinata》为演出收官。评论指出，尽管面临不适，Flórez凭借扎实的技巧与经验克服困难，呈现了一场赢得热烈掌声的开幕音乐会。

contents.en: The 87th Quincena Musical Donostiarra opened on 2 August 2026 at the Auditorio Kursaal in San Sebastián with a recital by Peruvian tenor Juan Diego Flórez and his regular pianist Vincenzo Scalera; tickets had been sold out well in advance after twenty-two years since Flórez's last appearance at the Kursaal. Although the tenor announced a recent throat ailment and used tissues, an inhaler and a small mysterious potion onstage, he chose to keep the concert, making minor cuts and one substitution to protect his upper register. The first half featured three Bellini songs, two Rossini ariettas and Donizetti's “Oh! Rammenta, bella Irene”; a planned cabaletta from La Cenerentola was replaced by the Rossini recitative and aria “O comme il fosco… Quell'alme pupille” from La pietra del paragone to avoid an extreme high note. The second half combined Spanish and French repertoire—numbers by Soutullo y Vert, Pérez Soriano and Serrano, Scalera's solo Mazurka “Glissando” by Ernesto Lecuona, followed by Massenet's “Pourquoi me réveiller?” and Gounod's “Ah, lève-toi, soleil,” in which Flórez delivered the three inevitable “si sobreagudos” mentioned in the review. Scalera's sensitive accompaniment and solo contributions (including Rossini, Lecuona and Godard pieces) were singled out for praise. For encores Flórez picked up a guitar to perform several popular songs—including Gardel's “Volver,” “La flor de la canela,” “Fina estampa” and “Cucurrucucú, paloma”—and Scalera closed the evening with Leoncavallo's “Mattinata.” Reviewers noted that, despite his vocal problem, Flórez relied on technique and experience to overcome the difficulty and delivered a warmly applauded opening concert.

articles.title: 拜罗伊特艺术节在克里斯蒂安·蒂勒曼指挥下庆祝瓦格纳《尼伯龙根的指环》150周年
articles.result: 拜罗伊特（27/07/26–01/08/26）在Bayreuther Festspielhaus上演瓦格纳《尼伯龙根的指环》，由Christian Thielemann担任音乐指导，Bayreuther Festspielhaus乐团与合唱团演出，合唱指挥为Thomas Eitler-de Lint。该制作以引入人工智能辅助的regie为卖点，策展人（curador）为Marcus Lobbes，艺术技术团队包括Nils Corte、Roman Senkl、Phil Hagen Jungschaeger、Andri Hardmeier、Wolf Guatjahr与Pia Maaria Mackert等。舞台由大幅循环幕（ciclorama）覆盖，投射由历届Ring制作档案与AI生成图像混合而成的动态画面；演员以破旧黑色服装出场，舞台基本空置，人物多为静态或以夸张的动作代替传统导演调度。观众在每部歌剧结束时以嘘声和喝倒彩表达不满，艺术团队在Götterdämmerung谢幕时遭遇长时间且强烈的抗议。该制作被评论为技术尝试未达预期，成为一次“失败的试验”；主办方宣布本Ring仅在今夏上演。音乐层面获得高度评价：Thielemann被赞为掌控Wagner色彩与戏剧细节的核心，尤其在Das Rheingold起始、整部四部曲的抒情与沉默处理上表现突出。主演中，低男中音Michael Volle的Wotan获得特别肯定；Klaus Florian Vogt在Loge、Siegmund与Siegfried三角角色中创下成为首位在四日内演出多角色的历史记录，但其声音风格与力量存在评论性的限制；芬兰女高音Camilla Nylund的Brünnhilde亦被视为重要亮点。报道同时回顾了拜罗伊特自瓦格纳时代以来作为技术与戏剧创新试验场的传统，并提及1976年Chéreau的Ring对节日史的重要影响。

contents.en: Bayreuth (27/07/26–01/08/26) staged Wagner's Der Ring des Nibelungen at the Bayreuther Festspielhaus, with Christian Thielemann as musical director. The Orchestra and Chorus of the Bayreuther Festspielhaus performed, with chorus master Thomas Eitler-de Lint. The production foregrounded the use of artificial intelligence in the regie; Marcus Lobbes acted as curator, supported by a technical and artistic team including Nils Corte, Roman Senkl, Phil Hagen Jungschaeger, Andri Hardmeier, Wolf Guatjahr and Pia Maaria Mackert. The staging used a large cyclorama projecting AI-generated montages drawn from the Festival's Ring archives; singers wore ragged black costumes and performed on an otherwise empty stage, often remaining largely static while the projections evolved. Audiences responded with whistles and boos at the end of each opera, and the artistic team faced prolonged and intense protest during the Götterdämmerung curtain call. Critics described the AI-led regie as a failed technical experiment and noted the production was announced to be presented only this summer. Musically the cycle was highly praised: Thielemann was credited with mastering Wagnerian color, drama and silence—from the opening of Das Rheingold through the lyricism that pervaded Die Walküre, Siegfried and the monumental Götterdämmerung. Cast highlights included Michael Volle's Wotan, singled out for artistic dignity; Klaus Florian Vogt, who performed Loge, Siegmund and Siegfried and became the first singer at the Festival to appear in roles across the four Ring days, though critics noted limitations in dramatic power; and Camilla Nylund as Brünnhilde was also noted as a major presence. The report also recalled Bayreuth's longstanding role as a laboratory for theatrical and technical innovation, and referenced Patrice Chéreau's influential 1976 Ring.

articles.title: 意大利指挥家布鲁诺·坎帕内拉去世，享年83岁
articles.result: 布鲁诺·坎帕内拉于8月4日去世，享年83岁。他被认为是近几十年意大利歌剧舞台传统的代表人物之一，名字自然与美声派曲目紧密相连，但其曲目也涵盖莫扎特、威尔第、布里顿、拉威尔和斯特拉文斯基等作曲家。坎帕内拉1943年1月6日出生于巴里，先后师从尼诺·罗塔和路易吉·达拉皮科拉学习作曲，随后跟随汉斯·斯瓦洛夫斯基和托马斯·希珀斯深造指挥。其职业生涯活跃于世界主要歌剧院——米兰斯卡拉、大都会歌剧院、伦敦皇家歌剧院、巴黎歌剧院、巴塞罗那利塞乌、马德里皇家乐团剧院以及都灵剧院（他曾在1992至1995年间担任该院音乐总监）——并在佩萨罗的罗西尼歌剧节中占有重要地位，参与了所谓的“罗西尼复兴”。他与阿尔弗雷多·克劳斯长期合作，曾有多部重要录音（如多尼采蒂的《军中女儿》，EMI）。后来他伴随胡安·迭戈·弗洛雷斯的国际崛起，再次录制《军中女儿》（Virgin，DVD）。其他著名录音还包括与切契利亚·巴尔托利合作的罗西尼《灰姑娘》（Decca）、与玛丽埃拉·德维亚在马德里皇家乐团剧院的《罗伯托·德韦鲁克》（BelAir，DVD）以及卡特琳·巴特的《美声咏叹调》（Deutsche Grammophon）。

contents.en: Bruno Campanella died on August 4 at the age of 83. He was regarded as one of the conductors who best embodied the tradition of Italian lyric theatre in recent decades, closely associated with the bel canto repertoire while also conducting works by Mozart, Verdi, Britten, Ravel and Stravinsky. Born in Bari on January 6, 1943, Campanella studied composition with Nino Rota and Luigi Dallapiccola and later refined his conducting with Hans Swarowsky and Thomas Schippers. His career took him to major opera houses worldwide — La Scala in Milan, the Metropolitan Opera in New York, the Royal Opera House in London, the Opéra de Paris, the Liceu of Barcelona, the Teatro Real in Madrid and the Teatro Regio in Turin, where he served as musical director from 1992 to 1995 — and he was a notable presence at the Rossini Opera Festival in Pesaro, participating in the so-called Rossini Renaissance. articles.result: 在拜罗伊特上演的理查德·瓦格纳歌剧《Rienzi》由指挥Natalie Stutzmann和导演Alexandra Szemerédy、Magdolna Parditka推出，引发热烈反响。Natalie Stutzmann认为《Rienzi》是瓦格纳后期音乐剧的重要前奏：虽然在宏大的配器和群体场面上仍属法国大歌剧传统，但已显露出成熟瓦格纳的音乐架构、半音和声、早期的主导动机萌芽及非凡的现代性，因而是“杰作”，其复杂的配器与对位写作预示了后来的风格。演出对指挥、乐队、合唱与独唱者在体力上要求极高，但参与者对作品的热情强烈。导演Szemerédy与Parditka并不将新版直接作为希特勒寓言，而是考察民粹化的权力机制，探问一位富有远见的政治家如何成为独裁者以及为何群众会被魅力型领袖吸引；作品的历史负载及与国家社会主义的关联被有意识地纳入思考，同时关注里恩齐与其妹妹的私人关系如何孕育权力与依附。舞台也融入自嘲性元素：一段芭蕾戏中以近似Monty Python的幽默短促引用瓦格纳歌剧。整场演出在乌托邦与反乌托邦张力中展开，并以呈现权力自我塑造及其毁灭性后果的画面收束。文章作者为Axel Brüggemann；BackstageClassical的文章为免费发布，文末倡导支持独立古典音乐新闻。

contents.en: The Bayreuth production of Richard Wagner’s Rienzi, led by conductor Natalie Stutzmann and directors Alexandra Szemerédy and Magdolna Parditka, has drawn enthusiastic response. Stutzmann regards Rienzi as a decisive step toward Wagner’s later music dramas: though the work’s monumental forces and mass scenes place it in the tradition of French grand opéra, it already shows features of the mature Wagner—clear musical architecture, chromatic harmony, early signs of leitmotifs and an unusual modernity—and she calls it a “masterpiece,” with orchestration and contrapuntal design that foreshadow his later work. The performance is physically demanding for conductor, orchestra, chorus and soloists, yet all participants show great enthusiasm. The directors do not present the new staging as a direct Hitler parable but as an examination of populist power mechanisms, exploring how a visionary politician becomes a dictator and why people are seduced by charismatic leaders; the production consciously considers the work’s historical burden and connections to National Socialism and emphasizes Rienzi’s private relationship with his sister as a source of power and dependency. The staging includes self-ironic touches—a ballet scene briefly quotes Wagner’s operas with allusions to Monty Python-style humor—and the evening moves between utopia and dystopia, ending with an image that links the self-staging of power to its destructive consequences. The article is by Axel Brüggemann; BackstageClassical’s articles are free and the piece encourages support for independent classical journalism.

articles.title: 黄领带：儿子眼中的塞利比达切
articles.result: 电影《黄领带》由塞利比达切之子塞尔盖·伊恩（绰号Miki）执导，剧本为他与詹姆斯·奥利弗共同创作，2025年上映。影片通过多段情节与回忆呈现罗马尼亚指挥家塞尔吉乌·塞利比达切的生平与性格，重点描绘他与专制父亲的复杂关系、近乎病态的自我要求、以及对录音的顽固反对。片中有标志性场景：1989年费城指挥布鲁克纳第四交响曲尾段后指认观众并因听到暗录而愤怒；两年后在法国与日本唱片公司代表（影片虽未点名但明显暗指索尼）就数字化复制与巡演版权发生激烈冲突。影片并呈现他与柏林爱乐的冲突、在保罗·福特温格勒与卡拉扬时代的复杂关系，以及他在战后试图影响乐团选人和拒绝录音的经历。评论指出影片并不美化人物：既表现了他的完美主义、对音色与排练的苛求及与禅宗的关联，也展示了其傲慢和对学生与同僚有时粗暴的态度；但片中对他对现象学思想的阐述较少。影评人还提到一个未在片中详细说明的事实矛盾：尽管片中强调他拒绝录音，塞利比达切生前曾授权索尼以影像光盘形式发布他与慕尼黑爱乐的部分布鲁克纳演出，片尾仅提到其遗产持有人授权EMI与DG发行会场录音的CD。主演阵容包括本·施内策（青年塞利比达切）、约翰·马尔科维奇（年长塞利比达切）、伊万·霍罗克斯（孩童时期）、西恩·宾（Demostene Celibidache）、凯特·菲利普斯（妻子Ioana）、米兰达·理查森（年长Iona）、查理·罗（Miki）等。影片曾于去年秋季在西班牙短暂放映，但据影评人所知尚未在西班牙在线平台上线，也未被配音。总体评价为对人物的有力刻画与出色表演，兼有戏剧化处理与对若干矛盾的回避。

contents.en: The Yellow Tie, directed by Sergiu Celibidache’s son Sergei Ioan (known as Miki) and co-written with James Olivier, was released in 2025. The film traces Romanian conductor Sergiu Celibidache’s life through episodes and memories, focusing on his fraught relationship with an authoritarian father, an almost pathological self-demand for perfection, and his stubborn opposition to recordings. Key scenes include a 1989 Philadelphia performance of the coda of Bruckner’s Fourth where the older Celibidache (played by John Malkovich) reacts to clandestine recording, and a subsequent meeting in France with Japanese executives—implied to be from Sony—where he adamantly rejects digital exploitation of concerts. The film also dramatizes his conflicts with the Berlin Philharmonic, the complicated context around Furtwängler’s return and Karajan’s later election, and his postwar attempts to influence musician selection and ban recordings. Reviewers note the film does not soften his image: it portrays his perfectionism, insistence on sound and meticulous rehearsals, and affinity with Zen, as well as his arrogance and sometimes harsh treatment of students and colleagues; it gives little space to his phenomenological approach. Critics also point out a notable omission: although the film emphasizes his refusal of recordings, Celibidache had authorized Sony to release several Bruckner concerts on LaserDisc during his lifetime, while the end credits only mention posthumous CD releases by EMI and DG authorized by his heirs. The cast includes Ben Schnetzer (young Celibidache), John Malkovich (older Celibidache), Ewan Horrocks (child Celibidache), Sean Bean (Demostene Celibidache), Kate Phillips (Ioana), Miranda Richardson (older Iona) and Charlie Rowe (Miki). The film screened briefly in Spain last autumn but, according to the reviewer, has not appeared on Spanish streaming platforms nor been dubbed there. Overall it is judged a strong portrait with fine performances, alongside some dramaturgical liberties and avoidance of certain contradictions.

articles.title: 萨尔茨堡 / Theodor Currentzis 指挥的电声版《卡门》
articles.result:
地点：萨尔茨堡，Großes Festspielhaus；日期：2026年8月3日。演出作品：乔治·比才《卡门》。指挥：Theodor Currentzis；舞台导演：Gabriela Carrizo（Peeping Tom）。主演：Asmik Grigorian（卡门）、Jonathan Tetelman（唐·何塞）、Kristina Mkhitaryan（米凯拉）、Davide Luciano（埃斯卡米洛）、Iveta Simonyan（弗拉斯基塔）等。合唱与乐团：Bachchor Salzburg、Salzburger Festspiele und Theater Kinderchor、Utopia orchestra。

舞台与概念：Carrizo呈现现代化、去陈词滥调的舞台，但做出关键性改动——删除对白，改以电声中场和舞台哑剧衔接剧情。评论指出此举造成两方面问题：一是叙事连续性被打断，音乐段落有时显得戏剧上断裂；二是歌唱者无法充分展开角色心理，整台戏显得单调、缺乏戏剧张力，除最终二重唱外紧张感有限。Carrizo试图通过一名女配饰演母亲（Eurudike De Beul）来深化唐·何塞的心理，并以歌手Amparo Cortés将Lilás Pastia民俗化（她以卡门的“Chanson bohème”开场并表现优秀），但评论认为这些“更西班牙化”的尝试意义有限。评论还提到作者梅里美笔下的《卡门》更多关于法国人的视角，而非西班牙本身。

音乐与表演：Theodor Currentzis及其为之打造的Utopia orchestra带来了高度技术性的演绎，萨尔茨堡观众给予热烈掌声与起立致敬。起始前奏曾令人期待一场难忘演出，但随后的指挥处理被评为技术上精湛却缺乏戏剧连续性，部分归因于舞台删节与电声插段；亦有质疑其对“Chanson bohème”先极慢后狂速的处理为噱头且并不原创（评论提及Maazel有类似处理）。

独唱表现方面，Asmik Grigorian被评为非凡艺术家，虽纸面上似非典型卡门，却在舞台上充分占有角色，中心唱区色彩充足且表演力强，但对白被删使其人物刻画不完整；其“信件场景”被视为全剧最佳片段。Jonathan Tetelman以较法式的处理和半声细节令人惊艳，声线偏spinto但具英雄金属感，并在咏叹调中按谱以钢琴弱唱出降B音，被评论赞赏；最终二重唱声势强劲，但导演对唐·何塞的过度幼稚化处理影响了表演。Davide Luciano被认为是有魅力且声乐慷慨的埃斯卡米洛；Kristina Mkhitaryan展现抒情且细腻的米凯拉，但在无对白的设定下人物显得被削弱。Iveta Simonyan的弗拉斯基塔获得好评。合唱与合奏在合唱与重奏段落配合良好，Bachchor Salzburg和儿童合唱亦获称赞；Currentzis时常让部分乐手起立演奏，作为一个效果化手法。

Place: Salzburg, Großes Festspielhaus; date: 3 August 2026. Work: Georges Bizet, Carmen. Musical director: Theodor Currentzis; stage director: Gabriela Carrizo (Peeping Tom). Principal cast: Asmik Grigorian (Carmen), Jonathan Tetelman (Don José), Kristina Mkhitaryan (Micaëla), Davide Luciano (Escamillo), Iveta Simonyan (Frasquita), plus Anita Monserrat, Matthias Winckhler, Liviu Holender, Michael Arivony, Mingie Lei. Choirs and orchestra: Bachchor Salzburg, Salzburger Festspiele und Theater Kinderchor, Utopia orchestra.

Staging and concept: Carrizo offered a modernized production that strips many Spanish clichés but made a decisive change by removing spoken dialogue and inserting electroacoustic interludes coupled with pantomime. The review highlights two problems caused by this choice: it breaks narrative continuity so Bizet’s numbers sometimes proceed with dramatic incoherence, and it prevents singers from developing characters’ psychology. The result was judged monotonous and lacking dramatic intensity, with tension appearing mainly in the final duet. Carrizo attempted to probe Don José’s psychology via a mother figure on stage (Eurudike De Beul) and to folklorize the piece by featuring cantaora Amparo Cortés—who opened the “Chanson bohème” successfully—but the critic found such “authentically” Spanish additions ultimately sterile and recalled that Carmen often says more about the French perspective than about Spain.

Music and performances: Currentzis and his Utopia orchestra brought notable technical excellence; the Salzburg audience received him warmly. His impressive opening prelude raised expectations, but his conducting was ultimately judged as technically superb yet lacking dramatic continuity, a defect partly attributed to the staged cuts and electroacoustic interludes. Questionable choices included extreme tempo shifts in the “Chanson bohème” (very slow then frantic), viewed as showy and not original (the critic cites Maazel’s similar practice).

Soloists: Asmik Grigorian was praised as an extraordinary artist—perhaps not the ideal Carmen on paper but fully inhabiting the role, with an appropriately colored middle and strong acting—yet the removal of dialogue left her portrayal incomplete; her cards scene was singled out as the opera’s high point. Jonathan Tetelman impressed with a French-inflected approach, effective use of half-voice, and a spinto tenor with heroic timbre; he delivered the B-flat in the aria piano as written and sang the final duet with striking power, though Carrizo’s infantilizing of Don José clouded his interpretation. Davide Luciano was a charismatic, vocally generous Escamillo; Kristina Mkhitaryan a lyrical, delicate Micaëla whose character suffered from the lack of dialogue. Iveta Simonyan’s Frasquita was noted as excellent. Ensemble numbers were well coordinated; Utopia orchestra and choirs worked well under Currentzis, and both Bachchor Salzburg and the festival/theatre children’s choir received praise.

articles.title: 辱骂观众也不是解决办法，Ersan Mondtag先生
articles.result: 摘要：作者报道，奥地利萨尔茨堡的《Ariadne auf Naxos》首演在莫扎特之屋（Haus für Mozart）结束时遭到大规模嘘声。导演Ersan Mondtag在事后于Instagram转发了两则故事帖：一则写着“Provinzpublikum at Salzburger Festspiele”，另一则为对其作品的赞扬。作者批评Mondtag将观众的否定解读为“不称职”或“外行”，认为这是用权力话语否定评价的做法，并强调嘘声本身是一种参与和认真态度：观众对歌唱演员报以掌声与喝彩，但当舞台设计者上台亮相时响起嘘声。文章并对Mondtag的舞台处理提出具体批评：将作品移至“火星”并置于超级富豪宫殿，首幕被认为较为成功，但第二幕被指向塑料化美学、过度性化与持续动作，削弱了情感表达。作者援引歌剧史例证指出，1912年首版失败后，Richard Strauss和Hofmannsthal并未将失败归咎于观众，而是改编并于1916年在维也纳推出现有版本。文中还提到Mondtag将来可能在维也纳上演《尼伯龙根的指环》（Ring），并引述业内关于Kirill Serebrennikov原计划与相应制作可能转移的说法。作者以在Felsenreitschule上演的Messiaen《Saint François d’Assise》（由Romeo Castellucci和Maxime Pascal执导）为例，称其对观众的信任和严肃对待赢得了热烈回应，主张对到场者应有“尊重”而非简单寻求认同。文章最后列出萨尔茨堡艺术节此前一季约256,600名观众来自88个国家、上座率98.4%的数据，并署名作者Karl Keller及其背景简介。

contents.en: Summary: The article reports that the premiere of Ariadne auf Naxos at the Haus für Mozart in Salzburg ended with a large wave of boos for director Ersan Mondtag. Mondtag reposted two Instagram stories that night—one reading “Provinzpublikum at Salzburger Festspiele” and another praising his own staging. The author criticizes Mondtag for dismissing the audience’s reaction as lack of authority or competence, arguing this treats criticism as illegitimate and misuses the director’s greater communication resources. The piece notes that the audience applauded the singers but booed when the director and his team appeared. The author describes Mondtag’s production choice to set the opera on Mars in a super‑rich palace: the prologue worked for the reviewer, while the second part was criticized for excessive plastic aesthetics, sexualized clowning and constant motion that reportedly overwhelmed intimate moments and emotional clarity. The article recalls that the Ariadne version known today resulted from Strauss and Hofmannsthal reworking a failed 1912 Stuttgart version into the 1916 Vienna version, arguing that creators should continue refining rather than blaming audiences. It also reports that Mondtag is slated to stage the Ring in Vienna and mentions insider talk that Kirill Serebrennikov’s Ring might be reassigned, which the author views critically. As a contrast, the author cites Messiaen’s Saint François d’Assise at the Felsenreitschule (directed by Romeo Castellucci with Maxime Pascal) as an example of trusting the audience and receiving strong applause. The article concludes with Salzburg Festival statistics—about 256,600 visitors from 88 countries and 98.4% occupancy last summer—and includes the author’s byline and brief bio: Karl Keller, Zurich-born, piano studies and master’s in musicology, working as assistant conductor and composer.
